theater: Southern Italy Hidden Terrain & Volcanotectonics (Mount Etna, Campi Flegrei, Calabria, Apulia)
compliance: Rule e2s-014 Certified (Zero Synthetic Noise, Authentic GFS Tensors, Explicit origin='upper')

it_mount_etna.name: Mount Etna (Summit & East Flank Collapse)
it_mount_etna.significance: Highest active stratovolcano in Europe (3357m); East flank instability slipping towards Ionian Sea along Pernicana fault combined with central magma reservoir intrusion.

it_campi_flegrei.name: Campi Flegrei Caldera (Pozzuoli / Solfatara)
it_campi_flegrei.significance: Active volcanic caldera experiencing intense bradyseismic ground deformation (>8 cm/yr uplift) centered on Pozzuoli harbor, driven by hydrothermal-magmatic fluid pressurization.

it_aspromonte_sila.name: Aspromonte & Sila Crystalline Massifs
it_aspromonte_sila.significance: Steep crystalline granitic/metamorphic escarpments rising to Montalto (1955m) and Botte Donato (1928m); extreme slope instability, deep-seated landslides, and torrential fiumare runoff.

it_apulia_karst.name: Alta Murgia & Salento Karst Basin
it_apulia_karst.significance: Extensive Mesozoic carbonate karst plateau with dolines (Pulo di Altamura), sinkhole collapse subsidence bowls, subterranean drainage voids, and flash flooding in karstic lame.

it_catania_simeto.name: Catania Coastal Plain & Simeto Alluvial Basin
it_catania_simeto.significance: Major alluvial flood basin at the foot of Mount Etna discharging into the Ionian Sea; vulnerable to severe Mediterranean tropical cyclones (Medicanes) and radar backscatter specular drop (< -16.5 dB).

it_vesuvius.name: Somma-Vesuvius Volcanic Complex
it_vesuvius.significance: Iconic stratovolcano (Gran Cono 1281m) within the older Monte Somma caldera wall; dense peri-volcanic urban risk zone, summit subsidence, and hydrothermal tremor deformation.
